very_short.a: A computer is an electronic device that accepts data, processes according to instructions, and produces output. Main characteristics: speed, accuracy, storage, automation, diligence, versatility.

very_short.q: 2. Give two examples of input devices.
very_short.a: Keyboard and mouse are common input devices.

very_short.q: 3. Name any two permanent storage devices.
very_short.a: Hard disk and USB flash drive (or CD/DVD) are permanent storage devices.

short.a: Garbage In Garbage Out — incorrect input produces incorrect output; correct input produces correct output.

units.summary: Chapter 2 9 Figure: Abacus An abacus consists of a rectangular frame carrying a number of wooden rods. Its mid- bar divides each of these rods into unequal - upper and lower frames. The upper frame is called heaven, whereas the lower frame is called the earth. Heaven consists of two beads, whereas the earth part consists of five beads to each rod. The value of bead on heaven part is five and the earth is one. Calculation is done by moving the beads – up and down in the rod and counting them. Napier Bone Napier's bones are a manually-operated calculating device created by John Napier. Napier's Bones are numbered rods to help work different multiplication problems. He used bones to demonstrate division by subtraction and multiplication by addition, according to the principle of logarithms. He also published the table of logarithms in 1614 AD. Digital Computer Digital computer operates on discontinuous data like 0 and 1. It operates by counting and calculation. Its accuracy is high. It usually has high storage capacity. It is a general- purpose computer. Figure: Digital Computer Desktop PC, and Laptop are the examples of digital computer. 3. Hybrid Computer Hybrid computer has the combined features of both analog and digital computer. It can operate on both continuous and discontinuous data. It can convert analog data into digital and vice-versa. It is a special purpose computer. Mouse Mouse is a small hand-held pointing and clicking input device used to control the position of the cursor on the screen. It is a small plastic box with two or three buttons on the top. Two rotating wheels inside the mouse detect the movement and the direction of the movement. By pressing the mouse button, the user communicates his/her choice to the computer. The mechanical mouse consists of a ball on its underneath, that translates the mouse movement into digital signals. This mouse contains 1-3 buttons.
